newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia government strong poll lead melting away.
newsitem.headline: Australia government strong poll lead melting away.

text.p: The conservative Australian government's commanding opinion poll lead over the Labor opposition dramatically narrowed in the latest polls on Tuesday, with one survey showing both sides now even.

Race row politician Pauline Hanson's new One Nation Party has wooed voters away from Prime Minister John Howard's Liberal-National coalition, polls in The Sydney Morning Herald and The Australian newspapers showed.

Both polls reinforce recent commentary that Hanson's three-week-old party was threatening the Australian Democrats' position as the third major party in Australian politics.

"... Yet another opinion poll has confirmed that support for Ms Hanson has not faded away but has in fact begun to show signs of firming into an electoral force at least as strong as ... the Democrats," the Herald said in an editorial.
One Nation's support was two points ahead of the Democrats in both polls.
The Australian's poll showed the government's primary vote, before preferences, has slipped four points to 41 percent and Labor's has increased two points to 39 percent.
The Australian survey put One Nation's support at seven percent, up three points from the last poll two weeks ago.
The Herald poll, which included One Nation for the first time, put the government's primary vote at 38 percent, down six points in a week, and Labor's at 34 percent, down two points.
The coalition won power last year with a primary vote of 47.3 percent against Labor's 38.8 percent.
Under Australia's electoral system, parliamentarians must win a majority of votes.
To achieve this, ballots for candidates with the lowest support are redistributed according to preferences marked by the voter until one candidate passes the 50 percent mark.
Both newspaper polls interviewed voters around the country by telephone from May 2 to 4. The Herald poll quizzed 1,032 people and the Australian's 1,152.
